title: Long-term clinical follow-up in post-acute infectious syndrome
summary:
The PAIS-Follow-Up study is being conducted to better understand the long-term course of SARS-CoV-2 and other infections. In this study, blood samples (whole blood, serum, plasma, and urine samples), results of clinical tests (e.g., handgrip strength measurement, MoCA test, 1-minute sit-to-stand test, Schellong test, or 10-minute passive standing test), diagnoses, previous findings, and questionnaires completed during the clinical presentation(s) were recorded and analyzed. Blood and urine samples were not collected for the sole purpose of the study. In addition, samples collected during the clinical presentation will not be examined beyond the routine examinations performed during the clinical presentation. 

In order to better understand the health outcomes, progression, utilization, and factors influencing the long-term course of post-acute infectious syndrome, questionnaires will be administered at each visit. Follow-up appointments at our outpatient clinic are scheduled as needed and as capacity allows. In addition, written follow-up questionnaires will be administered after 6-9 months and every 12 months during the course of the study, if necessary.

interventions.name: This is a cohort study: a registry will be set up to enrol consecutive patients after acute COVID-19 disease or other infections who have persistent symptoms in the sense of a post-acute infection syndrome. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The prospective analysis from the date of approval will include all consenting patients who have had SARS-CoV-2 infection or any other infection consistent with the symptoms leading to presentation and who give written consent to be included in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
Lack of legal capacity, lack of consent, execution of sentence, patients < 18 years of age.
